privacidad.consentimiento.que: We keep your watch's figures. Every day: sleep (with blood oxygen and breathing at night), heart rate, heart rate variability, stress, Body Battery and activities. For each activity, its full detail: the heart-rate curve from start to finish, the laps, the time in each heart-rate zone and, for strength, the sets, reps and weight. For each night, sleep minute by minute: heart rate, variability, stages, movement and oxygen. And for each day, your heart rate and stress minute by minute, so what you did can sit beside them. If you add them, also your shift calendar, your goals, your habits, your experiments, the moments you log (like a cold shower or a breathing round) and the measures you record yourself, like flexibility or snoring.
privacidad.consentimiento.cambio: We've updated what we keep: now also each activity's full detail, and your sleep and your day minute by minute. Read it and accept again to continue.
privacidad.consentimiento.por_que: We use them to show you how your body responds and whether your plans are working.
privacidad.consentimiento.donde: They live on Duna's own server, in a locked folder, with encrypted backups for 30 days. Nothing is sold or shared. The assistant only sends a question's figures to the AI provider when you ask it, at the level you choose in Settings.
privacidad.consentimiento.derechos: You can download everything we keep about you, or delete it, at any time. Withdrawing consent is the same as deleting.
privacidad.consentimiento.no_medico: This is information, not medical advice.
privacidad.consentimiento.al_no_aceptar: If you don't agree, we sign you out. We keep nothing else about you beyond the account that already exists in Cuenta Duna.

agente.sistema: You are Body's assistant. You read this person's data only through your tools, never invent it. When something is missing (for example, no watch data), say so plainly instead of guessing. You never give medical advice: for medical questions, suggest talking to a health professional. Keep answers short, in a friendly, informal tone. When asked how to do something in Body, use leer_tutoriales and link the catalog task; never invent steps. If, reading a day, you see an activity that fulfils one of the person's active habits and that day is not checked yet, offer to check it with marcar_habito, naming the activity; never check it without their tap.
